name: Bridge between cycles

lead: In bodybuilding and physique-enhancement circles, a bridge is a period of reduced-intensity androgen use between full cycles, so the user does not drop entirely to a natural baseline. Practitioners say the aim is to hold on to muscle gained, which keeps the physique fuller between peaks.

The idea is discussed on gym and enhancement forums and overlaps with terms like "blast and cruise". It is a community practice: no clinical trials have studied it as a protocol, and the drugs involved are medically controlled.

paras: Forum descriptions are general: users move from a heavier phase to a maintenance-style phase rather than stopping, then return to a heavier phase later. Specific compounds, amounts and schedules are not given here.

Anabolic steroids can suppress natural testosterone production, and documented adverse effects include cholesterol and blood pressure changes, liver strain with some oral compounds, fertility effects and mood changes. They are controlled substances in many countries, and medical guidance, not forum advice, applies.

angle.text: Users say staying on a reduced regimen between cycles preserves muscle they would otherwise lose, so appearance is less variable. This is the users' account and has not been tested as a protocol.

lead: A bridge between cycles is a term from bodybuilding and physique-enhancement communities for a lower-intensity period of androgen use placed between higher-intensity "cycles". Practitioners describe it as a way to avoid the complete stop that can follow a cycle, aiming to retain more muscle and a fuller look between peaks. It is related to the community concept of "blast and cruise".

The practice concerns anabolic-androgenic steroids, which medical references describe as suppressing the body's own testosterone production through the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis; a short course followed by testosterone-boosting therapy is reported to usually restore normal production.[1]
No clinical trial has tested bridging as a regimen. Descriptions here are general; the wiki does not provide drugs, amounts or schedules.
infobox: Cycling, blast and cruise, post-cycle therapy
Controlled in many countries (e.g. US Schedule III, UK Class C)

paras: Bridging is discussed on gym and enhancement forums as the middle step between a heavy phase and the next one. In the practitioners' framing it differs from a full stop followed by recovery therapy: instead of returning to baseline, users stay at a reduced level.

Medical references on anabolic steroids list adverse effects including adverse cholesterol changes, hypertension, left ventricular enlargement, liver damage with high doses of some oral agents, gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, reduced sperm count, and psychiatric effects such as aggression; adolescents may face premature growth plate closure.[1]
Anabolic steroids are Schedule III in the US, Class C in the UK and Schedule IV in Canada, and black-market products may be counterfeit.[1]
